about: Hand-written science facts for the location knowledge. Every fact has a source. 'scope' says how local it is: 'area' = true for the boxwork area (not tied to this exact spot), 'ground' = true for this kind of ground (ridge, hollow, layer).

sources.jpl2026: NASA/JPL, 'NASA's Curiosity Rover Sees Martian Spiderwebs Up Close', 23 Feb 2026
sources.waypoints: Curiosity rover waypoints (JPL MMGIS), sol and position of each stop

area.text: Boxwork ridges are 1 to 2 m tall with sandy hollows between them, a web that stretches for kilometres.
Groundwater flowed through fractures and left minerals that hardened the ridges; wind later wore away the softer rock in between.
Finding boxwork this high on Mount Sharp suggests groundwater lasted longer than expected, giving life more time.
The boxwork sits in a layer rich in salty sulfate minerals.

stops.why_it_matters: Starting point: the boxwork ridges begin just south of here.
stops.look_for: Look south: the ridges form a web of low walls.
stops.curiosity: Curiosity entered the boxwork area here in July 2025 (sol 4596).

stops.why_it_matters: Each ridge marks a crack where groundwater once flowed.
stops.look_for: A dark line running along the top of a ridge.
stops.curiosity: Curiosity confirmed that these dark lines are fractures, supporting the idea that groundwater moved through them.

stops.why_it_matters: The ridge rock was hardened by minerals from groundwater.
stops.look_for: The dark central fracture along the ridge top. Photograph it from both sides.
stops.curiosity: Curiosity drilled a ridgetop in this area; X-ray analysis found clay minerals in the ridge.

stops.why_it_matters: Hollows are where wind removed the softer rock, and where Curiosity's wheels slipped in sand.
stops.look_for: Small round nodules on the ridge walls and the hollow floor.
stops.curiosity: Curiosity found nodules along ridge walls and in hollows but not near the central fractures; why is still unexplained.

stops.ground: ridge and hollow side by side
stops.why_it_matters: Comparing ridge and hollow rock shows what the water changed.
stops.look_for: Pale ridge rock next to the darker hollow floor. Take one sample from each.
stops.curiosity: In this area Curiosity drilled a ridgetop, a hollow and the transition between them: clay minerals in the ridge, carbonate minerals in the hollow.

stops.why_it_matters: The sulfate layer records Mars drying out over time.
stops.look_for: Layered, light-toned rock beyond the last ridges.
stops.curiosity: After the boxwork, Curiosity continued into the sulfate-rich layer (from sol 4820, February 2026).
